Join our Qrew!
We are seeking an experienced Senior LNG Originator to identify, develop, and execute LNG sale, purchase, and trading opportunities across our global portfolio. Based in either Singapore, London or Houston (with preference for Singapore), this role will lead complex commercial negotiations, build and manage senior-level relationships with suppliers, buyers, and portfolio players, and help shape the origination strategy for our LNG business. The successful candidate will work closely with trading, legal, shipping, risk, and regulatory teams to structure and close high-value, long-term and medium-term LNG transactions.
The LNG Originator I/II/Sr responsibilities include but are not limited to:
Lead the identification, development, and execution of LNG sale, supply, and trading opportunities, including long-term and medium-term contracts and portfolio optimisation initiatives.
Shape origination strategy and market entry approaches, drawing on market insight and an established network of counterparties across Atlantic and Pacific LNG basins.
Provide commercial leadership on complex, high-value negotiations — setting strategy, leading counterparty engagement, and securing favourable terms on pricing, risk allocation, flexibility, and optionality.
Originate and manage a portfolio of counterparties, targeting both established and new markets to grow trading volumes and margin.
Oversee contract structuring and finalisation, partnering with Legal and Risk to ensure alignment with commercial objectives and regulatory requirements.
Build and maintain senior-level relationships with key LNG suppliers, buyers, portfolio players, and strategic partners, acting as a primary commercial point of contact.
Work closely with the Trading, LNG & Origination desks to assess portfolio fit, short- and medium-term exposure, and value of prospective deals.
Prepare and present deal proposals, market analysis, and business cases to senior management and investment/commitment committees.
Monitor global LNG and gas market fundamentals, pricing dynamics, and regulatory developments, translating insight into actionable commercial recommendations.
Mentor junior origination and trading staff and contribute to the broader development of the origination function.
Required Experience and Skills:
5-10+ years of experience in LNG Origination, with a track record of leading and closing complex transactions.
Demonstrated network of counterparties across LNG buyers, sellers, portfolio players, and shipping/infrastructure stakeholders.
Experience negotiating SPAs, master trading agreements, and other long-form LNG/gas commercial contracts.
Prior exposure to deal structuring, pricing mechanisms, and risk allocation in LNG sale and purchase agreements.
Experience working cross-functionally with Trading, Legal, Shipping, Risk, and Finance teams.
Skills & Attributes
Strong commercial acumen with the ability to originate, structure, and close deals independently.
Excellent negotiation, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with credibility at senior/executive level.
Sound quantitative and contractual skills; comfortable with financial modelling and deal economics.
Self-motivated, resilient, and able to operate with autonomy in a fast-moving, global market.
Cultural fluency and comfort working across time zones with teams in London, Singapore, Houston, and other regional offices.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in business, finance, engineering, energy economics, or a related field; MBA or relevant postgraduate qualification is a plus.
Fluency in English required; additional languages relevant to target markets (e.g. Japanese, Korean, Mandarin, Spanish) are advantageous.
Location Notes:
London: role sits within the Commodities: Origination division and reports into a US-based VP-Business Development & Origination, working closely with counterparts in Singapore and Houston.
Singapore: role reports into a US-based VP-Business Development & Origination within the Commodities: Origination division, with close coordination with London and Houston offices.
Houston: role sits in EQT's Houston office with global travel required
Selected incumbent will be placed into the position that best suits their abilities and experience level.

We are looking for Data Analyst (CRM), to join our team in Barcelona.
At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.
What Will You Do
The CRM Analyst is the measurement and intelligence engine of the central CRM organization. Operating across all game titles, this person pulls, verifies, and reports on campaign performance; tracks trends; and ensures experimentation is structured to produce reliable, actionable results. Critically, they look beyond individual game performance to surface portfolio-wide segment insights - understanding how key player cohorts like VIPs, regular customers, new players, and conversion targets perform across the full game catalog.
Campaign Reporting & Performance
Pull and verify campaign data from the CRM platform and downstream analytics systems, reconciling any discrepancies
Produce regular campaign performance reports for each game team and portfolio-level summaries for the Director of CRM
Track trends over time — open rates, click rates, conversion, retention impact — and flag anomalies or degradation
Create and maintain dashboards that give CRM/Lifecycle Lead PMs visibility into the performance of their communication programs
Experimentation Design & Governance
Support CRM/Lifecycle Lead PMs in designing A/B and multivariate tests, ensuring appropriate sample sizes, holdout groups, and clean control conditions
Maintain an experimentation log across all games to prevent conflicting tests and ensure results can be interpreted confidently
Review proposed experiments for methodological soundness before launch
Analyze and present experiment results with clear, actionable recommendations
Cross-Portfolio Segment Insights
Define and maintain segment definitions across the portfolio (e.g., VIP, Regular Customer, New Player, Lapsed, Conversion Candidate)
Track how these segments behave and respond to CRM across multiple titles, identifying patterns and outliers
Produce regular cross-game segment reports that help the Director of CRM and game teams understand what works universally versus what is title-specific
Identify high-value segment opportunities that are underserved by current campaigns
Data Integrity & Targeting Validation
Validate that targeting attributes used in campaigns are correctly populated and reliably representing the intended audience
Partner with Data Engineering to surface data quality issues and advocate for fixes
Verify that audience sizes match expectations prior to campaign launch
What We’re Looking For
4+ years in marketing analytics, CRM analytics, or a related data role - ideally in a behavior-based vs transactional environment - like gaming or live services.
Proficiency with SQL and at least one BI or reporting tool (e.g., Looker, Tableau, Mode, or equivalent)
Experience working with CRM or marketing automation platforms to extract and interpret campaign data
Experience with both performance data and attribution data and able to ensure appropriate tracking is in place.
Ability to represent data needs to engineers if necessary data options are not available.
Understanding of A/Bn testing methodology, statistical significance, and experiment design across a complex set of overlapping campaigns.
Ability to communicate data findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Experience in games, apps, or a retention-driven consumer product is a strong plus
Comfortable managing multiple reporting workstreams simultaneously across different game teams
Experience in gaming as a player or operations manager preferred.
Technical Skills
SQL (required)
Excel / Google Sheets (advanced functions, pivot tables)
BI tools (Looker, Tableau, Amplitude, etc.)
Familiarity with event tracking tools (Segment, Snowflake, BigQuery, etc.)
Basic understanding of data pipelines and data quality checks

Role Overview
As our Staff Data Analyst for Pricing and Retail Analytics, you will be at the forefront of our data-driven decision-making process. Your responsibilities will include ensuring the quality of regular reports and metrics, driving impactful insights, and supporting system-wide decision-making algorithms across key business areas. You will also collaborate with fellow analysts on the team, shaping the direction of reports, metrics, and system algorithms to meet business goals. Your work will directly inform business strategy and influence key product and operational decisions.

Design, develop, and maintain decision-making systems, focusing on pricing strategies. Analyze data to identify trends and drive business insights.
Continuously improve Pricing/Promotion reports and systems, staying updated on new technologies and ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
Contribute to strategic planning with data insights, helping to shape metrics, product features, and business strategies.

Strong understanding of statistical analysis and algorithm design. Ability to apply this knowledge in the context of business data to deliver actionable insights.
Demonstrated ability to think systematically and maintain clarity in documentation. Proven track record of managing multiple tasks and projects simultaneously, with a strong focus on structure and organization in both analytical thinking and the documentation of processes, methodologies, and results.
Ability to understand business goals and translate them into actionable data strategies. Strong product sense to guide data analysis that shapes business decisions, operational goals, and product features.
Strong problem-solving capabilities with the ability to navigate ambiguity. Proactive in identifying and resolving issues, continuously improving processes, and driving results in a dynamic environment.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Proven ability to engage with stakeholders at all levels and present complex data insights in a clear and accessible manner.
A self-starter with natural curiosity, a strong sense of ownership and urgency. Comfortable working independently and managing projects in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment.

8+ years of industry experience in business analytics and Master’s or PhD degree in quantitative field
Previous experience in a retail, e-commerce, or similar fast-paced, data-driven environment. Familiarity with pricing strategies, retail commerce, and promotions
Familiarity with big data technologies like Hadoop and Spark, along with experience in workflow orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow) and version control systems (e.g., GitHub).

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Enterprise Knowledge Work team builds the products that help enterprise knowledge workers collaborate deeply with Claude for major parts of their work.
Over the past year, AI has transformed how software engineering happens; for the rest of knowledge work, though, using AI still mostly means answering questions and producing first drafts — a small slice of the actual job.
We're building toward something bigger: people and agents working together on every core work objective, from first idea to finished product, and the recurring work of a team running with Claude in the loop instead of a person pushing every step. It's an enormous space, it's early, and no one has built it well yet.
You'll help decide what these products are, not just how they're built — the product questions are as open as the architecture ones — and you'll see your work land with real teams at the world's largest enterprises.

Own technical design and delivery for enterprise-facing core products, end-to-end across the stack
Partner with product, design, and go-to-market to turn enterprise customer workflows into shipped product, not just execute against a spec

Work directly with enterprise customers and sales during key conversations, translating what you learn into engineering priorities
Work closely with research to make the models better in your domain: shaping evals, surfacing failure modes, and feeding customer learnings back into model development
Mentor other engineers and raise the technical bar across the team, working with influence rather than authority
Build the core primitives that enable knowledge workers across industries and roles to meaningfully leverage Claude

Have 8+ years of software engineering experience, ideally with 2+ years at a Staff or equivalent technical leadership level
Have led the design and delivery of complex customer-facing products across the full stack
Have built AI products and know what it takes to turn model capabilities into applications people actually use
Are comfortable working directly with enterprise customers and translating what you learn into technical decisions
Have built products from 0 to 1 in fast-moving environments, and can set technical direction with limited precedent to lean on
Drive cross-team alignment to ship impactful work, with influence over authority

jobs.description: Amazon cannot fix a customer experience problem it cannot measure. Our team's job is to make shopping quality measurable: to find the defects customers actually encounter, quantify how often they encounter them, and put a number in front of leadership that teams are willing to be held to. Today that capability is strongest on the search results page, where we run a portfolio of quality metrics covering areas such as relevance, duplication, and brand quality, backed by a mix of human annotation and LLM based measurement. We are hiring a Sr. Product Manager - Technical to own the quality bar for core shopping: the standard that defines what counts as a customer visible defect, how precisely it must be measured, and what evidence is required before a number can be trusted. You will drive alignment on that standard across the organizations whose experiences it judges. Owning the bar is the job. Measurement and inspection are how you enforce it: you will own the quality metric portfolio for the search page, the inspection mechanisms that surface the defects we are not yet measuring, and the scalable mechanisms (human annotation, LLM based evaluation, and the audit loops that keep both honest) that hold the system together as coverage grows. You will expand that coverage beyond search to other core shopping surfaces, including the Homepage and Detail Page. Key job responsibilities Define the quality bar: - Own the standard that every metric definition, annotation SOP, and automated measurement approach must satisfy before it can be trusted or published. Scientists, engineers, and annotation partners build to that bar. - Own the portfolio of shopping quality metrics against that bar, covering areas such as relevance, duplication, and brand quality, and grow that portfolio as new defect classes are identified. Own the inspection mechanisms - Own how we find quality defects, not just how we count the ones we already know about: sampling strategy, audit cadence, anecdote review, and systematic inspection of pages customers actually saw. - Turn qualitative signal into quantified metrics. Work with UX Research and leadership to convert customer anecdotes and research findings into defect definitions that can be sampled, scored, and tracked. - Own the audit loop and the SOP bar. Specify what gets audited and against which criteria, review findings, and require the resulting corrections in annotation SOPs or LLM prompts. When a measurement approach systematically misses a defect class, you own defining what the corrected standard is, and the team builds to it. Drive quality measurement into online systems - Drive the agenda to move quality measurement from offline, after the fact reporting into online systems, so that quality signals are available where experiences are ranked and served rather than only in a periodic report. - Partner with central platform teams to embed quality metrics into online evaluation and serving paths. - Make the case for where online quality signals change decisions, including experimentation guardrails, faster detection of quality regressions, and closed loop correction of defective experiences. Own the roadmap - Own the multi year roadmap for shopping quality measurement and inspection: which defects to measure next, which surfaces to expand to, and what each expansion unblocks for the business. - Extend the charter beyond search to other core shopping pages, starting with Homepage and Detail Page. For surfaces with no measurement today, define the defect taxonomy from scratch: what a quality defect is on that page, how it is sampled, how it is scored, and how it rolls up. - Drive alignment across Organic Search, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and International as definitions evolve, including with the teams whose experiences the metrics judge. About the team The mission of the Core Shopping Data Science team is to provide the data-driven foundation for building a world-class shopping experience that maximizes long-term free cash flow by delighting customers. We focus on the long term and big picture to ensure that the full Amazon shopping experience balances strategic trade-offs. We believe data science is the discipline of making smart decisions and we empower feature owners and systems by 1) developing and vending metrics which assess and value customer engagement, 2) building tools and datasets to inject data into the decision-making process, and 3) delivering deep analyses to inform high-touch decisions.

jobs.description: Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most. What you'll work on: • Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover. • Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable. • Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers. • RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope. • System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit. Key job responsibilities What we look for: • Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware. • Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it. • Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system. Our stack: Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. A day in the life As part of our BSP software engineering team, you will design and implement embedded software used in the Project Kuiper products. You will work in a collaborative environment with teams inside and outside of Amazon. You will craft your software from requirements, designs, code, test, to product deployment. You need to be flexible and responsive to changing priority issues. About the team The Kuiper Customer Terminal Software Team supports the devices that connect our customers to the Kuiper network. We provide software for both applications and the underlying Linux system. We work hand in hand with hardware, product and operations teams to deliver a great experience for our customers.
